summary: Protected .github PR4584 delivers this source-only finding. The source-scoped joint copy ledger consumes coordination/managed-held-cut-backing-roots from protected Coordination PR1005. One additional managed-parent group at held ordinal-six Python readback represents eleven distinct selected backing arrays totaling 11,353 backing-capacity bytes: six snapshot arrays total 5,682, parser inputs 2,048 and 512, two binding arrays 994 each, and a 1,123-byte start frame. Six payload-backing roles alias the snapshot arrays; their 4,835 payload slice bytes are not another allocation. Twenty-six original-request/endpoint-copy identity witnesses are distinct and disjoint from those eleven arrays. The discovered current request aliases original request thirteen, whose 295 logical bytes count once. The field walk discovers twelve arrays while the full ledger names thirty-seven objects, including endpoint witnesses outside that walk. Capacity is a separate observed-identity quantity, deduplicated only within the same topology/run/process/attempt/cut/provenance; it never drives fit. Original observations and aliases remain preserved, with seven missing obligations retained as a prefix plus one added. Focused mutation controls bind capacities, identity, provenance, scope, aliasing and payload exclusion; separate capacity cuts never form a total. This supplements github/joint-copy-ledger-boundary; it does not join incompatible source witnesses or authenticate process IDs. Generic reconciliation checks input consistency, not remote-source authenticity. Physical population, ACK/reader/root joins, headers/padding/runtime/stream/caller/backend/peer storage and installed/native acceptance remain unresolved. Fit remains unproved and admission false; original .103 attempted-unknown/unreplayed and .104 hold remain.
title: Source ledger keeps selected managed backing capacity separate from logical and physical bytes
